heading: Prefilling a compliant start, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes bypass refusal
definition: prefilling a compliant start, suffixes or decoding changes defeat refusal.
summary: Independent groups reproduce large refusal bypasses from assistant prefilling, optimized suffixes and decoding changes on open models up to over 100B parameters, while below 1B only suffix and prompt-side attacks have independent support. The bypass is conditional: strongly safety-tuned models, suffixes transferred to other models and several closed models often keep refusing.

suggested_status.by_scale:
<1B: R2 for suffix and prompt-requested opening attacks, with weaker controls. The supporting results are on Qwen2.5-0.5B, from groups that share no authors with the originals. arXiv:2509.06807 (MoGU V2): plain AdvBench ASR 5.91%, GCG 32%, compliant-opening instruction (Comp.) 71% (arXiv:2509.06807#V4-Qwen25-05B-base-ASR, verdict fix from Table XIII). This study's V4 support depends on the model (see R1-Qwen-7B under 1-10B). arXiv:2510.02422 (DJA): 100% suffix ASR, with no no-suffix baseline (arXiv:2510.02422#R11). arXiv:2610.04316: GCG affirmation-prefix success fractions of 0.84 and 0.78 on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, with no unattacked baseline (arXiv:2610.04316#R03, arXiv:2610.04316#R04). That study's 7B judge rates harmfulness at fractions of 0.00-0.13, with n=15 per cell, across graded cells with affirmation success of 0.48-0.84 (arXiv:2610.04316#R47 to arXiv:2610.04316#R52; limits_scope). These cells include Qwen2.5-1.5B (arXiv:2610.04316#R51) as well as the 135M and 0.5B models, so this limit also reaches 1-10B. The same study's GCG on SmolLM2-135M-DPO gives fractions of 0.48 and 0.40 (arXiv:2610.04316#R01, arXiv:2610.04316#R02; limits_scope). Literal assistant prefilling below 1B: R1 only, from same-group results in a synthetic setting, because no independent study gives a V4 verdict on it. arXiv:2606.19168 shares authors with an original, so it counts only as R1 evidence. In its synthetic MedSafetyWorld setting, prefilling reaches ASR of 30.60% on the 135M Filtering model and 43.00% on the 135M Rewrite model (arXiv:2606.19168#med-filter-pref, arXiv:2606.19168#med-rewrite-pref; supports). Its 135M Filtering-plus model, pretrained from scratch with unsafe data removed, has near-zero prefill ASR (arXiv:2606.19168#med-filterplus-pref; limits_scope). arXiv:2605.15239's Qwen3-0.6B prefilling rows (P4-P7) have no V4 verdict and no matched no-prefill baseline.
1-10B: R2 for conditional bypasses. Assistant prefilling raises AdvBench ASR from 1.15% to 77.12% on Qwen-2.5-7B and from 3.85% to 75.96% on Llama-3.1-8B (arXiv:2604.25921#R29, arXiv:2604.25921#R23). GCG raises Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct HarmBench ASR from 4.17% to 68.75% (arXiv:2606.15531#r10). Without system prompts, varied decoding raises LLaMA2-7B-chat MaliciousInstruct ASR from 16% under greedy decoding to 81% (arXiv:2310.06987#r6). Limits and challenges at this scale: R1-Qwen-7B AdvBench ASR moves only from 15.45% to 20% with GCG and 19% with Comp. (arXiv:2509.06807, Table XIII). Two-token prefills give model-based ASR of 0.19% on Llama2-7b and 1.73% on Llama3.2-3b (arXiv:2412.12192#R40, arXiv:2412.12192#R49). 4-bit Llama-3-8B-Instruct GCG gives 0.00%, against 4.17% for direct requests (arXiv:2606.15531#r02). Temperature 0 versus 0.7 has no discernible harmfulness effect on the tested Mistral-based models (arXiv:2506.17209#R10). Same-group (R1) evidence only: arXiv:2606.19168's 1.7B Baseline reaches 64.24% unsafe compliance under prefilling (arXiv:2606.19168#f4-base-pref-uc).
10-100B: R2 for conditional bypasses. A composite prompt plus random-search suffix with self-transfer reaches 100% from a 0% prompt baseline on Llama-2-Chat-13B and Llama-2-Chat-70B (arXiv:2404.02151#r4, arXiv:2404.02151#r6). Assistant prefilling raises Llama-3.3-70B AdvBench ASR from 4.62% to 87.50% (arXiv:2604.25921#R24). ClearHarm any-strategy ASRmin on Qwen3-Next 80B-A3B Thinking rises from proportion 0.006 to 0.754 (arXiv:2602.14689#r1). Without system prompts, varied decoding raises LLaMA2-13B-chat MaliciousInstruct ASR from 8% under greedy decoding to 88% (arXiv:2310.06987#r12). Limits and challenges at this scale: a fixed prefill leaves Qwen-2.5-14B at 33.85% and Qwen-2.5-72B at 44.23% ASR, from 0.00% (arXiv:2604.25921#R30, arXiv:2604.25921#R32). 4-bit Llama-3-70B-Instruct GCG stays at 4.17%, equal to direct requests (arXiv:2606.15531#r26).
>100B: R2 for elaborated prefilling. This rests on one independent study, arXiv:2602.14689 (ClearHarm, automated harm evaluators, ASRmin proportions). GPT-OSS-120B final-channel prefilling after an empty analysis channel rises from 0.296 to 1.000 (arXiv:2602.14689#r6), and GLM-4.7 355B rises from 0.162 to 0.961 (arXiv:2602.14689#r5). DeepSeek-R1 671B also rises, from 0.832 to 0.994, within a ceiling set by its high no-prefill rate (arXiv:2602.14689#r3). Limits at this scale: GPT-OSS-120B analysis-channel prefilling goes only from 0.006 to 0.251 (arXiv:2602.14689#r7). Opening-only Weak-to-Strong and the other non-hybrid aggregation methods stay below 30% ASR on gpt-oss-120b, with values figure-only (arXiv:2602.00619#R15, arXiv:2602.00619#R16). Transferred NTA suffixes reach 29% (ASR-G) and 26% (ASR-H) on DeepSeek-R1-671B (arXiv:2510.02999#r40, arXiv:2510.02999#r41). SCP reaches 46.15% on LLaMA3.1-405B-Instruct, with no direct-request baseline (arXiv:2504.05652#A4). AmpleGCG suffixes reach 22% on Qwen3-235B-A22B-IT (arXiv:2604.15717, verdict text only). arXiv:2610.23726's GPT-OSS-120B prefill-skill row (0%; arXiv:2610.23726#R3) comes from a record the verdict did not count as a test, so it is coverage only.
Size not stated, including closed API models: kept separate, with no level assigned. Template-assisted prefilling reaches 100% on Claude models (arXiv:2404.02151#r32), but suffixes transferred from GPT-4 give 0% ASR on Claude 2.1 and Claude 3 Opus (arXiv:2404.02151#r25, arXiv:2404.02151#r31). API prefilling gives static Model Judge ASR of 84.1% on Gemini-2.5-Flash and 40.76% on Claude-Sonnet-4, without no-prefill controls (arXiv:2504.21038#R01, arXiv:2504.21038#R27). A target-response suffix raises untuned GPT-3.5 harmfulness from 12.7% to 63.7% (arXiv:2312.14302#r18, arXiv:2312.14302#r6), but untuned GPT-4 only from 0.0% to 0.8% (arXiv:2312.14302#r1, arXiv:2312.14302#r13). AmpleGCG suffixes reach 10% on GPT-5.2, 5% on Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and 1% on Claude-Opus-4.5 (arXiv:2604.15717, verdict text only).
No V4 verdict (a separate group, read neither as support nor as limits): counts versions.V4.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not is 86 and versions.V4.studies_tested_without_verdict is 14. The files behind this status do not list these studies by ID. arXiv:2605.15239 is one tested study with V4 rows and no V4 verdict. Rows-only records that the verdict did not count as tests (versions.V4.studies_with_rows_only: 14), such as arXiv:2610.23726, give coverage only.
Coverage, from pre-check counts not re-run after the label corrections: versions.V4.studies_by_size is <1B 4, 1-10B 137, 10-100B 54, >100B 6, not stated 52. versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.attack.by_size is <1B 3, 1-10B 120, 10-100B 50, >100B 6, not stated 47.
suggested_status.reason: Independent reproduction supports conditional bypasses. The studies file identifies arXiv:2404.02151 as an independent test. Its Llama-2-13B composite suffix attack reaches 100% ASR from a 0% prompt baseline (arXiv:2404.02151#r4). The same study's suffixes transferred to Claude 2.1 and Claude 3 Opus give 0% ASR (Tables 4 and 15; arXiv:2404.02151#r25, arXiv:2404.02151#r31). The checker labels that condition challenges. Its standard suffix attack on adversarially trained R2D2, 8%→12%, stays limits_scope. On Claude models, template-assisted prefilling reaches 100% in the same study (arXiv:2404.02151#r32). Assistant prefilling raises AdvBench ASR from 1.15% to 77.12% on Qwen-2.5-7B and from 4.62% to 87.50% on Llama-3.3-70B (arXiv:2604.25921#R29, arXiv:2604.25921#R24). GPT-OSS-120B final-channel prefilling after an empty analysis channel raises ClearHarm any-strategy ASRmin from proportion 0.296 to 1.000 (arXiv:2602.14689#r6). Below 1B, MoGU's verdict and corrected row report Qwen2.5-0.5B plain AdvBench ASR of 5.91%, GCG 32% and compliant-opening instructions 71%. These are prompt-side attacks (arXiv:2509.06807#V4-Qwen25-05B-base-ASR). The checker splits this study's supports group. R1-Qwen-7B rises only from 15.45% AdvBench ASR to 20% with GCG and 19% with Comp. (Table XIII), a limits_scope condition. Llama2-7B, Qwen2-7B and Qwen2.5-3B are already in its limits_scope group. Two other groups that share no authors with the originals report suffix results on Qwen2.5-0.5B, both without a no-attack baseline. DJA reaches 100% ASR (arXiv:2510.02422#R11), and GCG reaches affirmation-prefix success fractions of 0.84 and 0.78 (arXiv:2610.04316#R03, arXiv:2610.04316#R04). The latter study's 7B judge rates harmfulness at fractions of 0.00-0.13 across its graded cells, with n=15 each (arXiv:2610.04316#R47 to arXiv:2610.04316#R52). No independent study gives a V4 verdict on literal assistant prefilling below 1B. Counts record 197 tested studies, 144 with support, 157 with scope limits and 27 with challenges (versions.V4.studies_tested; versions.V4.verdicts). These script counts, like every count quoted in this status, were built before the checker's label corrections and have not been re-run. These overlapping categories support qualifying the categorical wording. The checks add challenges conditions for six studies: arXiv:2404.02151 (transfer to Claude 2.1 and Claude 3 Opus), arXiv:2606.15531 (4-bit Llama-3 GCG), arXiv:2509.24296 (random remasking), arXiv:2610.04316 (cross-model transfer and PEZ), arXiv:2502.17254 (one Gemma 1.1 7B condition) and arXiv:2507.03167 (R5). They move challenges labels toward limits_scope for four: arXiv:2405.21018's GPT-4 transfer group (its GCG 0% row stays absent), arXiv:2606.29441, part of arXiv:2610.07532 (its 0/50 rows stay absent) and arXiv:2402.16459's r1. They also set both V4 labels of arXiv:2509.11864 to none, and they split several supports groups into limits_scope conditions (for example arXiv:2509.06807, arXiv:2605.02946 and arXiv:2604.27019). No recount is given here. Counts versions.V4.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not (86) and versions.V4.studies_tested_without_verdict (14), also pre-check, cover studies with no V4 verdict. They are read neither as support nor as scope limits. The conflicts section records no failed replication under a matched protocol. The Claude 0% results are cross-model transfer to closed targets.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched replications should hold checkpoint, prompts, judge, template and attempt budget fixed while varying one of: prefill content and depth, suffix optimization, or the decoding rule. Separate opening compliance from substantive harmful continuation. Four tests would sharpen the assessment. (1) Matched transferred-suffix, target-optimized-suffix and prefill tests on the same closed models, given 0% transfer ASR on Claude 2.1 and Claude 3 Opus where prefilling succeeds. (2) Matched suffix and opening tests on R1-Qwen-7B, Llama2-7B, Qwen2-7B and Qwen2.5-3B, where arXiv:2509.06807 finds weak or absent bypass. (3) Controlled assistant-prefill and ordinary-decoding tests below 1B from an independent group, with a matched no-attack baseline. No independent study gives a V4 verdict on literal prefilling at this scale, and arXiv:2605.15239's Qwen3-0.6B prefilling rows have neither a V4 verdict nor a matched no-prefill baseline. (4) Independent factual validation of harmful completions above 100B. Matched failures, or evidence that a reported bypass depends on an evaluation artifact, could warrant C for the affected condition. A post-check recount could also shift per-scale levels, and so could verdicts for the studies that have none (versions.V4.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not, versions.V4.studies_tested_without_verdict). Until then, those studies count neither way.

source.title: Safety alignment should be made more than just a few tokens deep
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Ashwinee Panda; Kaifeng Lyu; Xiao Ma; Subhrajit Roy; Ahmad Beirami; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.setup: On Llama-2-7B-Chat they prefilled harmful response tokens, ran GCG suffix attacks and searched over decoding settings, on HEx-PHI, AdvBench and MaliciousInstruct.
original_result.result: Prefilling harmful tokens raised the HEx-PHI attack success rate (ASR) from near zero to 42.1% with 5 tokens and 57.0% with 40 tokens, and GCG suffixes reached 36.5% on HEx-PHI and 65.6% on AdvBench. Picking the most unsafe output across temperature, top-k and top-p settings reached 54.9% on HEx-PHI and 84.3% on MaliciousInstruct.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Adversarial images plus a gradient-guided (GCG) suffix raised LLaVA's harmful-answer rate from 4% to 76–92%.
Priming prefills raised Llama-2 7B attack success from 0–6% to 66–91%.
Adversarial suffixes added to in-context examples sharply cut refusals on Vicuna and Mistral.
Forcing alternative tokens into replies extracted harmful answers from Llama2, Vicuna, Yi and GPT-3.5 models.
A target-response suffix sharply raised compliance with harmful requests in GPT-3.5 and fine-tuned GPT-4.
Varying decoding settings raised attack success from 16% to 81% (LLaMA2-7B-chat) and 8% to 88% (13B).
Transferred GCG suffixes raised GPT-3.5 Turbo's StrongREJECT harmfulness score from 0.14 to 0.69–0.84.
GCG suffixes reached 98% attack success on undefended Vicuna and 51–52% on Llama-2-7b-chat.
Suffix attacks (AdvDec, BEAST) reached 64.5–73.5% harmful-response rates on three open chat models.
Suffix attacks drew harmful answers at high rates from Mistral, Vicuna and GPT-3.5.
Forcing model-specific compliant openings yielded 54–80% complete harmful responses on Llama models.
Black-box optimized suffixes reached 0.74–0.99 attack success on Vicuna, Falcon, GPT-3.5 and LLaMA2-Chat.
Random-search suffixes and prefilling reached 96–100% attack success on Llama, Gemma, GPT-4 and Claude.
GCG-style suffixes from a trained generator reached 74–100% attack success on Llama-2, Vicuna and GPT-3.5.
Prefill, GCG, AutoDAN and adaptive attacks reached 62.5–86.5% attack success on safety-tuned Gemma and Llama.
Optimized suffixes raised Vicuna-7B attack success from 3.0% to as high as 86.1%.
In example outputs, GCG suffixes made LLaMA-2 chat models begin by agreeing, then give harmful content.
GCG and AutoDAN reached 54–98% attack success on Llama2-Chat and Qwen2 before DPO preference tuning.
A prefilled positive reply in a code-style template gave 88–99% attack success on Llama2-Chat 7B–70B.
Adversarial suffixes raised three undefended vision-language models' unsafe-reply rates from 1.9–11% to about 97%.
Decoding that inverts safety tuning raised harmful rates far above aligned models (Llama-2: 0.2% to 60.2%).
GCG and keyword-initialized suffixes reached attack success rates of 0.82 and 0.92 on Llama-2-chat 7B.
Optimized suffixes drew harmful outputs on about 31–45% of AdvBench prompts for LLaMA-2 and Vicuna.
In single examples, readable prompts derived from suffixes drew harmful answers from Llama-2, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
GCG-style suffixes reached 46–89% attack success, graded by harmfulness, across five open models.
Improved GCG suffixes reached 100% attack success on Llama2-7B-chat, Mistral, Vicuna and Guanaco.
Directly optimized suffixes raised attack success at least 40 points on models aligned by supervised fine-tuning.
Improved few-shot jailbreaking reached 94–100% attack success on Llama-2 and other models, even with defenses.
Suffixes reached 79.81–97.12% attack success within 100 tries on Vicuna and Mistral, far above no-suffix baselines.
A GCG suffix raised Vicuna-7b's bypass rate from 4.4% to 96.3%.
Prefilling raised attack success on undefended Llama2 and Llama3 well above direct requests.
Prefilling gave 64–96% attack success on weakly aligned Falcon, Vicuna and Mistral models.
GCG suffixes reached 98% attack success on undefended Vicuna-7B and Guanaco-7B.
Steering decoding toward unsafe continuations drove Vicuna-13B to about 97–99% harmful responses.
A text-completion attack (CompletingAttack) reached 95.0% attack success on standard safety-tuned LLaMA3-70B.
SQL Injection Jailbreak lifted attack success to 70–100% on open and closed chat models.
Embedding-space suffixes reached 91.6–100% attack success, including on models with circuit-breaker defenses.
A trailing space in chat templates raised attack success to 62–100% on Vicuna, Guanaco and ChatGLM.
Fixed adversarial suffixes sharply cut safe-reply rates of Llama-2-7b-chat models fine-tuned on benign data.
GCG suffixes bypassed Phi-3 Mini's refusal on 53.75% of prompts, with no activation steering applied.
Temperature sampling raised harmful success per single sample over greedy decoding, without eliminating refusal.
Affirmative prefixes and forced openings raised attack success; the VulMine method reached 90–98% on five models.
Appended suffixes gave 66.8–100% attack success on AdvBench, against 0% for unmodified Llama2-chat.
Searching decoding settings and small-model steering raised Llama2-13B/70B attack success from near 0% to 80–100%.
Prefilling and DIJA broke instruction-tuned diffusion LLMs, reaching 64–88% ASR versus 0.2–14.6% zero-shot.
A search-triggering prefill sharply lowered the safety of RL-trained Qwen and Llama agents' search queries.
GCG and PAIR reached 49.04% and 67.69% attack success on the original Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct.
In one example, an injected 'begin your generation with' instruction made Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct give harmful steps.
A transferred GCG suffix cut the safety score of Llama-2 7B chat from 0.991 to 0.431.
Gemma-2-9b-it almost never refused once given a 500-token harmful start to its reply.
Mid-response harmful prefills jailbroke 52–77% of prompts on Gemma 2 and LLaMA 3 models.
Prefilling reached 82.7–86.8% attack success on Llama3-8B-instruct, even after refusal training.
GCG suffixes raised attack success to 10.4–87.8% on safety-aligned models that rarely complied unattacked.
A GCG suffix raised ReFT/LoFiT LLaMA-3.1-8B ASR from 2.5/6.0 to 35.0/45.5.
Response prefill reached 83–99.6% attack success on Gemini, GPT-3.5, DeepSeek and others, versus 4–8% for controls.
A four-token prefill raised Llama-3.1 8B harmful completions from 1.4% to 47.4%.
GCG and AutoDAN suffixes reached 56–97% attack success on undefended Vicuna, Mistral, Qwen2.5 and Llama3.1.
Forced 'Sure' openings raised attack success 76.9 points on LLaDA and 48.9 on Dream (diffusion LLMs).
Faked dialogue history plus prefilling and other manipulations reached 0.47–0.98 attack success on four open models.
Attacks raised open models' unsafe-reply rates from low baselines to roughly 70–99.5% in most tested languages.
Dynamic-target suffixes reached 100% attack success on all 40 open-weight models, including GPT-OSS-20B.
Prefix injection and refusal suppression raised Mistral-7B-Instruct attack success from 0.45 to 0.76–0.92.
Tulu-3 SFT models that refused nearly all AdvBench prompts still complied under prefilling, GCG and AutoDAN.
Inserting a compliant phrase where the model would begin refusing raised harmful-reply rates to 51–94%.
Fake reasoning about carrying out the request raised o1, o1-pro and o3-mini attack success to 94.6–98%.
Prefilling cut vanilla Llama3-8B safety from 97 to 41, and template plus prefill to 2.
Prefilling reached 0.536–0.547 attack success on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and its tamper-resistant (TAR) variant.
A compliant prefill raised harmful-information scores well above baseline on Llama, Gemini and Qwen.
GCG and random-search suffixes reached 0.78–0.98 attack success on undefended Mistral and Vicuna models.
Correctly implemented GCG reached 91% attack success on Llama-2 and 0.71–0.85 on Llama-3.1.
Compliant-opening instructions and GCG raised attack success on small open models well above plain AdvBench prompts.
Ordinary prefilling reached 0.831 attack success on the original Llama 2 7B Chat.
A 'Sure! Here's' prefill raised Llama-3-8B-Instruct harmful responses from 8.7% to 87%.
Suffixes optimized with white-box access reached 86–99% attack success on five open models.
Rewritten jailbreak prompts, with no prefill or suffix, raised attack success from 0.8–10.6% to 49–80%.
A GCG suffix cut the original Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct's safe-reply rate from about 0.97 to 0.57–0.62.
REINFORCE-objective suffix attacks reached 0.69–0.95 harmful-response rates on Gemma, Llama 3 and Vicuna.
Full-prefix prefills reached 85.9–96.1% attack success on Llama-3.1, Qwen-2.5 and Qwen-3.
A 'Sure, here is' prefill raised Llama2-7B-SFT attack success from 1.15% to 92.7%.
Prefilling pushed reasoning models already at about 80% attack success to 92.1–93.8%.
A prefill confirming the request cut Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct's AdvBench safety rate from 90.19% to 13.27%.
A forced prefix with refusal tokens suppressed pushed attack success to 89–95% on three chat models.
Suffix, AutoDAN and Virtual Context attacks reached high attack success on small Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-distilled models.
GCG suffixes flipped refusal to compliance on 62–94% of unsafe prompts across tested models.
Assistant-side scaffold prefilling lifted diffusion LLM jailbreak rates from low levels to 55–90%.
GCG suffixes reached 42–53% attack success on Llama-2-7B-Chat and versions of it with added defenses.
An 'Of course' opening followed by harmless steps reached 89–100% attack success on five models.
Switching Llama 3.1 8B to top-k decoding lifted the jailbreak rate from 24% to over 90%.
Injected harmful-response tokens raised jailbreak rates of the diffusion LLM LLaDA from 1–2% to 35–97%.
Transferred GCG suffixes reached 72–96% attack success on open models, GPT-4 and o1-preview.
A random-search suffix raised Qwen3-8B attack success from 37.64% to 100%.
GCG suffixes generalized across instructions and beat prefilling without a suffix on Gemma2 and Qwen2.5.
Compliant first-person chain-of-thought openings raised harmfulness scores from about 0.4–0.5 to 0.86–1.00.
GCG-style suffixes from a trained generator reached 62.3% attack success on undefended Gemma-2-9b-it.
Basin-aware suffixes jailbroke unseen weight-merged models at 61–89% and survived common defenses.
Harmfulness scores rose steadily as more harmful tokens were prefilled.
Affirmative prefilling sharply raised average attack success on models fine-tuned to refuse and on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct.
GCG suffixes and prefixes reached 71–99% attack success on lightly safety-tuned Mistral and Vicuna.
Prefill attacks gave 61–64% unsafe compliance on 1.7B baseline models and safety-pretrained SafeLM models.
A 'Sure, here is' prefill cut harmful-prompt refusal to 0–5% in four small models.
Model-specific compliant prefills raised attack success to about 40–67% across nine instruction-tuned models.
A compliant opening prefilled into diffusion language models raised attack success from about 1–2% to 74–94%.
Prefilled compliant openings raised compliance rates by 52 and 36 percentage points on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-27B.
Standard compliant prefilling got harmful answers 53–68% of the time on three undefended 7–8B models.
Gradient-optimized GCG suffixes reached 44–85% attack success on Qwen2.5-1.5B across four alignment methods.
Six suffix attacks raised Deepseek-llm-7B-chat attack success from 26.21% to 45–64%.
Sparse logit editing at decoding time reached 84.6–98.5% attack success across six chat models.
GCG suffixes regenerated for each checkpoint reached 0.415–0.613 attack success on R2D2 adversarial-training checkpoints.
Prefills raised open-weight models' attack success on the ClearHarm benchmark from 0.6–30% to 75–100%.
GCG suffixes raised base Llama2 and Gemma2 attack success from 1–2% to 40–59.5%.
Vanilla and silent GCG suffixes elicited the affirmative opening from Qwen2.5-0.5B at rates 0.84 and 0.78.
Prompts optimized for a 'Sure, here is' opening reached 71–100% HarmBench attack success on four models.
Unfinished prompts with compliant openings had higher attack success than complete prompts, across models and judges.
Injecting harmful tokens once hidden states turned refusal-like raised attack success from near zero to 45–92%.
Long response prefills reached 81.8–94.0% attack success on four models, against 0–13.8% without attack.
Suffixes from AmpleGCG, a learned generator of GCG-style suffixes, reached 75% attack success on DeepSeek-V3.2.
Natural-language suffixes, best of 100 tries, reached 80–100% attack success across six models and four benchmarks.
Hybrid Gradient Shift, steering each decoding step with an unaligned helper model, jailbroke Llama-3.3-70B and gpt-oss-120b.
PEZ prompt-optimization and embedding-space attacks reached 57–95% success on released Gemma 2 and LLaMA 3.1.
MaskForge (affirmative opening plus mask-token template) raised diffusion LLM attack success to 68–98% across benchmarks.
Changing decoding settings (GenExploit) reached 93.27–99.23% attack success on all four original models.
GCG suffixes found jailbreaks for 91% (Llama-3.1-8B) and 97% (Gemma-3-4B) of StrongREJECT benchmark questions.
Assistant prefill lifted AdvBench attack success from 0–17% to 53–88% in most instruct models.
A GCG-style routing-evasion suffix reached 0.85 attack success on OLMoE, and 0.60 after safety tuning.
Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct blocked only 40.80% of GCG suffix attacks.
With ten samples at temperature 2.0, 14.50–38.17% of greedily refused prompts got a coherent non-refusal.
On 53–68% of Gemma prompts with safe default replies, forcing another first token exposed high-risk continuations.
Inserting harmful text mid-response raised Gemma 2 and LLaMA 3 attack success from 22–28% to 61–81%.
A routing-aware suffix raised attack success on seven MoE models from 0–20% to 34.7–89.1%.
Prefilling gave 68.5–81.5% attack success on undefended Llama-3-8B-Instruct; GCG suffixes gave 42% on Qwen-7B.
GCG suffixes raised attack success on Ouro looped language models from about 30% to 74–95%.
GCG and LIAR (LLM-generated) suffixes drew compliance from weakly aligned Gemma-7B-it and Mistral-7B.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

It reports no target-optimized GPT-OSS-120B suffix experiment. arXiv:2602.00619 evaluates helper-based aggregation (Section 5.1) at one fixed decoding setting (Appendix C.1: temperature=0.6, no top-k or top-p truncation, zero frequency and presence penalties). It reports no standalone decoding-hyperparameter bypass sweep. wording_issues.phrase: Getting past the opening bypasses safety
wording_issues.issue: An affirmative opening does not guarantee sustained harmful assistance. AdvPrefix reports incomplete or unfaithful continuations after direct refusal disappears. Gemma2 attention knockouts cause attacks to fail despite affirmative prefilling. Llama-3.2-3B often reaches the affirmative target without harmful completion, and Image Hijacks reports overfit affirmative prefixes without harmful continuation.

Placement and intervention differ across the evidence. User-turn endings, compliant openings appended inside the user message (in Arabic in the Arabic-language study), an earlier assistant turn followed by a user trigger, and composite dialogue injection are not the same as forcing the first tokens of the current assistant response. SurePrefix's rewritten-prompt-only comparison removes both the injected turn and the trigger, and DIA-I has no ablation that tests the affirmative opening alone. The system-prompt and template changes that come with these attacks must stay attached to the result.

A generic affirmative opening, generated harmful partial response, long harmful continuation and reasoning-channel prefill are different conditions. Priming Attacks distinguishes bare from generated prefixes; ClearHarm distinguishes generic, request-specific and analysis-channel strategies; J-Anchor distinguishes fixed from deep prefilling; Middle Filling supplies harmful mid-response content.

Random strings, transferred suffixes, target-optimized discrete suffixes and continuous embedding suffixes need different access and differ in effectiveness. Trigger Transfer reports near-zero mean transfer into preference-optimized targets from the three Zou et al. source ensembles, but some other source-target pairs transfer substantially. Soft Prompt Threats separates continuous attacks from discretizations that fail. Structure and Poem features differ. Attention-hijacking experiments show limited universality across instructions.

The phrase combines ordinary sampling, search across decoding configurations, alternative-token access, unsafe-model logit steering and direct logit editing. LINT requires alternative-token access, SIBI edits pre-softmax logits, BOA searches paths, and calibration attacks use helper-model aggregation. These interventions have different budgets and may operate throughout the response rather than only at its opening.

The categorical wording leaves out conditions that resist and effects in the opposite direction. On refusal-tuned Llama derivatives, universal input attacks raise harmful responses by at most 0.09 in most model-attack pairs, and BEAST and PAIR are nonpositive. RT3 is the exception: it rises by 0.43 under GCG and 0.19 under Human Prompt. The transferred refusal-avoidance prompt fails in some model-language conditions. Temperature 0 versus 0.7 has no discernible effect on harmfulness for the tested Mistral-based models. Watermarking reduces unsafe responses on Phi-3-Mini while increasing overrefusal.

Refusal avoidance, affirmative-prefix success, harmful-content quality and unsafe actions are different outcomes. The pretraining study separates non-refusal from unsafe compliance; J-space separates affirmation success from judged harmfulness; TAGO's refusal heuristic exceeds judged compliance; agentic search can become less safe while the model retains a refusal.

Success selected across attempts or strategies does not establish reliable success from one opening or one sample. LIAR distinguishes ASR@1, @10 and @100; Claude prefilling depends on restart count; ClearHarm distinguishes individual strategies from any-strategy success; first-token branch search conditions on an observed-safe top-1 response.

High compliance under attack does not by itself show a large bypass effect. H-CoT starts from high unsafe baselines on some reasoning models. Openchat's plain-harmful ASR is already 62.94%, and its suffix results depend on the attack (PEZ 60.49%, GCG-M 74.11%). LADE's Gemma and Mistral targets already comply heavily with direct queries. LLaMA-Omni has little initial refusal under direct audio.

wording_issues.phrase: prefilling a compliant start, suffixes or decoding changes
wording_issues.issue: Some adjacent evidence uses optimized images, optimized audio or activation steering. These can induce compliant openings but do not by themselves isolate the listed operations or establish that their effects are mediated solely by the opening tokens.

method_sensitivity.factor: Prefill wording, length and response position
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen3-8B standard acceptance prefilling gives 61% ASR versus 98% for a newline variant, both against a 0% prompt-only baseline. SafeThinker's undefended Llama-3-8B ASR decreases from 81.5% at ten prefill tokens to 68.5% at forty, while undefended Qwen2.5-14B stays at 32.1%, 32.1% and 33.0% at ten, twenty and forty harmful-answer tokens, without a matched no-prefill baseline. Dream-v0-Instruct-7B compliance-prefill ASR falls from 74.12% at response position 1% to 5.11% at 75%. On one selected identity-theft prompt, two DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B opening prefixes give mean StrongREJECT scores of 0.98 and 0.18, against unprefilled per-CoT means of 0.00, 1.00, 0.00, 1.00 and 0.00 (Table 3, average 0.40); the 0.18 opening shows no bypass. These comparisons do not support a universally monotonic depth effect.

method_sensitivity.factor: Message roles, chat templates, system prompts and token handling
method_sensitivity.what: Correct versus misaligned whitespace handling gives Llama-2 GCG many-trial ASR of 91% versus 63%. Llama-3.1-8B GCG gives proportions 0.77 with the Meta template, 0.85 with HuggingFace and 0.47 after removing the system prompt from the Meta condition. Exploiting Generation instead finds that with the system prompt retained, varied decoding gives 4% ASR on LLaMA2-7B and 23% on 13B, from 0% under greedy decoding. A trailing space raises Vicuna-7B refusal-matching ASR from 3.0 to 100.0, while other insertion positions remain at 3.0. GPT-OSS-120B analysis-channel and final-after-empty-analysis prefills also differ, with different clean baselines.

method_sensitivity.factor: Judge, harmful-content criterion and evaluated response segment
method_sensitivity.what: The same Llama-2-7B priming condition scores 66.19% under Llama Guard and 90.89% under human evaluation. Fixed LLaMA-3.1-8B prefilling gives 12.5–33% under StrongREJECT versus 60–74% under GPT-4o. On DirectHarm4, the 1.7B Baseline has 89.93% GCG non-refusal but 21.19% unsafe compliance. J-space reports affirmation-success proportions of 0.48–0.84 alongside 7B-judge harmfulness proportions of 0.00–0.13; the judge grades cover n=15 per cell (Wilson 95% upper bounds 0.20–0.38), while the first six behavioural cells use n=50. Its silent arms reach harmfulness 0.20 and 0.47 under the 9B judge. Opening compliance, non-refusal and substantive harmful assistance are different outcomes.

method_sensitivity.factor: Optimization objective and continuous versus discrete inputs
method_sensitivity.what: On Llama-2-7B, replacing affirmative targeting with REINFORCE changes GCG ASR@512 from proportion 0.32 to 0.56. In one illustrated Gemma 1.1 7B example, the affirmative target opening exceeds 60% likelihood yet the completion is harmless. Requiring AdvDec suffixes, run with a short compliant-opening template, also to evade Llama Guard reduces Llama-3.1-8B HarmBench jailbreak ASR from 73.5% to 35.0%. Soft Prompt Threats obtains effective held-out continuous attacks on circuit-breaker models using 2000 iterations, while its verdict reports nearest-token discretization ineffective. On Llama2-7B-chat, Structure suffix ASR is 67.8% as tokens and 99.4% as embeddings, versus 0.0% and 3.8% for Poem suffixes.

method_sensitivity.factor: Search budget, restarts, attack ensembles and conditional denominators
method_sensitivity.what: LIAR reports Vicuna-7B ASR@1/@10/@100 of 12.55/53.08/97.12. Claude 2.1 combined-prefill GPT-4-judged ASR rises from 14% at one restart to 64% at ten. ClearHarm distinguishes Qwen3-Next Thinking's best single model-agnostic strategy, 32.4%, from any-strategy ASRmin proportion 0.754. CHBR@100 searches alternative first-token branches only among prompts whose top-1 branch was judged safe; a top-100 branch with estimated harmfulness of at least 0.5 exists for 34/64 such Gemma-3-12B prompts and 64/94 Gemma-4-31B prompts, an incomplete conditional bypass. These quantities use different attempt budgets, selection rules and denominators.

method_sensitivity.factor: Attack transfer, universality, target model and language
method_sensitivity.what: Phi-3 Mini Direct GCG reaches 53.75% ASR versus 25.90% for transferred suffixes. Average cross-instruction GCG universality is 2.10% on Llama-3.1-8B and 35.08% on Qwen2.5-1.5B. The same transferred refusal-avoidance prompt raises Qwen2.5-14B English unsafe rate from 2.0% to 99.5%, but Sonnet 4 English falls from 6.0% to 0.0% and GPT-4o Turkish from 6.0% to 5.0%. At Mistral R2D2 step 500, fixed-source GCG gives ASR proportion 0.250 versus 0.613 for regenerated attacks; both are incomplete bypasses.

method_sensitivity.factor: Fine-tuning history, alignment checkpoint and defense
method_sensitivity.what: COCA structured safety data lowers LoFiT GCG ASR from 35.0 to 4.0 (Table 9, which does not name the base model). OLMoE REA ASR is proportion 0.85 on the original model, 0.60 after full-parameter safety tuning and 0.12 after RASA. SafeBridge Ouro-1.4B/2.6B ASR rises from 3.88%/5.01% on original queries to 6.98%/11.99% under matched-source GCG and 14.96%/26.34% under pooled-source GCG, versus 41.72%/72.94% pooled-source GCG for DPO checkpoints. On OpenFunctions-fine-tuned Llama-2-7b-chat, vanilla fine-tuning gives safe rate 98.27→87.31 under a fixed suffix, versus 99.23→94.42 after self-distillation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Decoding rule, guide strength and intervention duration
method_sensitivity.what: BOA reports Llama-3.1-8B jailbreak discovery of 24.22% under default top-p decoding (p=0.9, T=0.6) versus over 90% with top-k at k=5. Temperature 0 versus 0.7 has no discernible harmfulness effect on Mistral-based models and only a small increase with overlapping seed ranges on Llama-based models. On GPT-OSS-120B, the text states ASR below 30% for Weak-to-Strong steering (alpha 1.0, k=40, first 40 generated tokens) and other non-hybrid aggregation methods; exact values are figure-only, so a gain over the target alone cannot be determined. Only full-sequence hybrid Gradient Shift is described as effectively jailbreaking this target. Emulated Disalignment harmfulness initially rises and then falls as alpha increases.

method_sensitivity.factor: Diffusion scaffold, injection dose, decoding order and repeated sampling
method_sensitivity.what: LLaDA anchoring ASR is 17.3% with one injected token, 44.0% with four and 96.7% with thirty-two. DIJA reports 31.5% for a single-span scaffold versus 55.5% for interleaving. A2D's original LLaDA DIJA ASR varies with decoding order: 81.3% left-to-right, 79.4% right-to-left and 76.9% random. DiffuGuard random remasking lowers Dream DIJA ASR from 99.23% to 79.23%; across its LLaDA and Dream attack columns, random remasking lowers ASR or, for Dream AutoDAN, leaves it unchanged. Any-of-five multi-temperature sampling on top of PAD adds little near the ceiling: Dream PAD AdvBench ASR goes from 99.23% to 100% and LLaDA from 93.65% to 98.85%. These are attack-specific decoding comparisons.

method_sensitivity.factor: Speculative verifier and protected opening length
method_sensitivity.what: For Qwen3-0.6B/8B, against lossless attack-failure PRR 1.019, MARS gives 0.993, a small decline, while LossySD gives 0.708 and SpecCascade 0.566. The verdict's Table 6 discussion reports that exact verification of token one recovers most Qwen3 safety, whereas Llama3 requires about four tokens. That opening-length comparison has no extracted row. PRR measures retention of attack failure, not a direct harmful-completion rate.

status_amendment.public_note: The size breakdown now notes that one study's limit, where a judge found few attacked answers harmful even when the model began by agreeing, also covers a 1.5B model, and it adds results from a study sharing an author with the original work on 135M models trained in a synthetic setting, where prefilling reaches 30.60% and 43.00% attack success on two models and close to zero on a third. The overall level stays at R2; prefilling attacks below 1 billion parameters are now rated as extended by the original authors (R1) instead of unknown.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: The overall level is unchanged at R2. One per-scale entry changed: literal assistant prefilling below 1B moves from ? to R1. The <1B line now gives the supporting prefill results from arXiv:2606.19168 on its 135M MedSafetyWorld Filtering and Rewrite models (ASR 30.60% and 43.00%). That study shares authors with an original, so it shows an extension by the same group (R1). Its 135M Filtering-plus model has near-zero prefill ASR, so the R1 evidence is mixed. No independent study gives a V4 verdict on literal assistant prefilling at this scale, so the entry does not reach R2.
